groups.name: The Office universe
groups.explanation: 'That's what she said.' (quote), Dunder Mifflin (location), Steve Carell (actor), and Threat Level Midnight (in-universe film title) are all from The Office (US).

groups.name: Fictional cities that were entirely destroyed or annihilated in their series
groups.explanation: Pawnee, Indiana (Parks and Recreation — nuked in a flash-forward finale), Caprica City (Battlestar Galactica — obliterated by the Cylons in the miniseries), Sunnydale, California (Buffy the Vampire Slayer — swallowed into a crater in the series finale), and Springfield (The Simpsons — repeatedly destroyed in 'Treehouse of Horror' episodes and The Simpsons Movie). Each fictional city is spectacularly destroyed within its own series.

groups.name: Characters who directly address the audience by breaking the fourth wall
groups.explanation: Cersei Lannister (Game of Thrones — in deleted scenes and certain stylized sequences), Francis Underwood (House of Cards — his direct-to-camera asides are a defining feature), Patty Hewes (Damages — narrates directly to the viewer in flash-forward framing), and Boyd Langton (Dollhouse — delivers a direct expository address to camera in the pilot). All four characters break the fictional frame to speak directly to the viewer.

groups.name: Characters who discover a shocking secret about someone they love — while sitting in a car
groups.explanation: Players will group these as 'characters connected to serial killers' or 'Dexter characters,' but the real connection is a pivotal car-scene revelation: Dexter Morgan (Dexter) learns Doakes is tracking him while driving; Camille Preaker (Sharp Objects) receives a devastating confession in a car at the finale; Nick Brody (Homeland) is confronted with evidence of his double life during a car ride; Hannah McKay (Dexter) discovers a critical secret about Dexter while in a vehicle. Each character's most world-altering revelation in their series is delivered in a car.
